script: JAX -2.5 and a 42 total set up a close, modest-scoring game, not a HOU comeback and not a shootout. JAX can stay on B.Tuten (54 carries, 218 yards over the last 3) while T.Lawrence throws; HOU's backfield is split (D.Montgomery and W.Marks both at 26 carries), so C.Stroud has to create rather than hand it to one back.
who_goes_off: B.Strange and J.Noel. Strange has 21 targets, 195 yards and 147 air yards in 3 games into a HOU defense allowing 9.43 YPA on 46 middle attempts. Noel has 10 targets, 143 yards and 106 air yards into a JAX defense allowing 9.59 YPA on 29 middle attempts, the only soft spot on a unit that holds rushers to 3.04 YPC.
weak_spot: Both pass defenses leak in the middle, not outside and not versus the run. JAX allows 9.59 YPA middle (29 att) versus 7.16 left (68 att) and 7.67 right (81 att), with only 5 runs of 10+ and 3.04 YPC. HOU allows 9.43 YPA middle (46 att) versus 5.41 left (56 att) and 7.25 right (75 att). That is LBs, nickel and safeties, not the outside corners.
injury_fallout: No injuries are in the pre-kickoff data, so the fallout is usage. Bri.Thomas has fallen to 7 targets and 25 yards over 3 games while B.Strange (21/195), P.Washington (17/171) and J.Meyers (15/134) have taken the JAX pass game. On HOU, N.Collins (15/174) and X.Hutchinson (16/162) still lead, J.Noel (10/143) is the intermediate riser, and F.Moreau is empty at 8 targets for 16 yards.
qb_vs_blitz: C.Stroud is 0.47 EPA/dropback vs blitz (n=42) and 0.02 with no blitz, and JAX blitzes 29%, so almost a third of his dropbacks are his best snaps and they favor J.Noel's intermediate answers. T.Lawrence is the reverse: 0.03 EPA vs blitz (n=48) and 0.37 with no blitz, and HOU blitzes only 20%, so he lives in the clean-pocket look that feeds B.Strange's 7-target pace.

picks.why: Strange is at 65.0 receiving yards a game (195 on 21 targets) versus a 37.5 line, with 147 air yards marking intermediate middle shots. HOU allows 9.43 YPA through the middle on 46 attempts and blitzes just 20%, which is Lawrence's 0.37 EPA no-blitz environment, and a -2.5 script does not require forcing Bri.Thomas (25 yards on 7 targets) back into the plan.

Noel is at 47.7 receiving yards a game (143 on 10 targets, 106 air yards) versus a 17.5 line. JAX's only soft pass location is the middle at 9.59 YPA on 29 attempts, while a 3.04 YPC run defense and just 5 runs of 10+ take away easy Marks/Montgomery yards. Stroud's 0.47 EPA vs blitz meets JAX's 29% blitz rate, so Noel's intermediate role is the answer, not a 17.5 projection.
